\newpage

\markright{\textit{Figure S1}}

\noindent{\fontsize{12}{14.4}\selectfont\textbf{Figure S1}}

\noindent{\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont\textbf{Decision-tree logic for classifying carcinogenicity from IARC group and GHS hazard statements.} Chemicals with a statistically significant difference in detection or abundance between thyroid tumor types were assigned a carcinogenicity category by integrating their International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC) group with Globally Harmonized System (GHS) hazard statements: H350 (``may cause cancer''), H350i (``may cause cancer by inhalation''), and H351 (``suspected of causing cancer''). Percentages denote the GHS consensus/confidence for the indicated statement as reported on PubChem (``GHS Classification'' subsection). Decisions are evaluated from top to bottom: a ``Yes'' assigns the adjacent category, while a ``No'' proceeds down the tree. IARC Group 1 and Group 2A assignments override GHS considerations. Any residual combination not otherwise resolved is assigned ``Uncertain Risk'', and chemicals with neither an IARC group nor a GHS carcinogen statement are considered Unclassified.}

\markright{\textit{Figure S2.1}}

\noindent{\fontsize{12}{14.4}\selectfont\textbf{Figure S2.1}}

\noindent{\fontsize{10}{12}\selectfont\textbf{Spectral validation of confirmed chemical identifications with type-associated differences in thyroid tumor samples.} Sample spectra for chemicals with statistically significant differences in detection or abundance across thyroid cancer types that passed manual spectral quality review, displayed either as mirrored plots with reference standard (sample intensity in positive y-axis, standard intensity in negative y-axis) or as non-mirrored plots without standard when reference co-elution was inadequate. Mirrored plots with co-elution of multiple fragments in both standard and sample are considered ``Level 1'' identifications (S2.1, pp. 5-25), while non-mirrored plots where multiple fragments co-elute in the sample but the standard does not show proper co-elution are considered ``Level 2'' identifications (S2.2, pp. 26-28). Asterisks (*) indicate the fragment used for statistical comparison and displayed in Figure 3 and/or Table 3. For select compounds, additional plots display isolated fragments for enhanced visualization clarity.}
